why: transfer() catches the post failure with a bare except and falls through to None, so settle_batch reads receipt_id off None and a dropped transfer leaves a hole in the ledger with no trace of the error
refills=[] is created once at import and shared by every call, so the second machine's refill plan comes back carrying the first machine's lines
product_id from the supplier feed is interpolated into an f-string passed to subprocess.run with shell=True, so a product id containing a subshell is executed by the label printer
the three chained .get() calls default to None when the export has no pricing block, and sum() raises TypeError instead of reporting zero revenue
the task returned by create_task is dropped, so a fetch that fails raises nowhere, is never retrieved, and can be collected before it runs
